title: ICU, Perioperative & Emergency Care
blurb: Detailed, de-identified records from intensive care units, operating rooms and emergency departments: vitals, labs, medications, notes and outcomes.

items.name: MIMIC-IV
items.full_name: Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV
items.description: The flagship open critical-care database: de-identified EHR data for patients admitted to the ICU or emergency department of Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Boston (2008–2019). Includes demographics, vitals, labs, medications, procedures, diagnoses and survival, organised in modular hospital (hosp) and ICU (icu) tables.
items.provider: MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology / BIDMC
items.access_note: PhysioNet credentialed account + CITI 'Data or Specimens Only Research' course + signed DUA. Also queryable on Google BigQuery.

paper.label: Johnson AEW et al. Sci Data 2023;10:1

items.name: MIMIC-III
items.full_name: Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III
items.description: The predecessor of MIMIC-IV covering ~46,000 ICU patients at BIDMC (2001–2012), including bedside charting, labs, medications and >2 million free-text clinical notes. Still the most cited ICU dataset and the basis of many benchmarks.
items.provider: MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology / BIDMC

paper.label: Johnson AEW et al. Sci Data 2016;3:160035

items.name: MIMIC-IV Clinical Database Demo
items.description: A 100-patient subset of MIMIC-IV with identical structure, released openly so anyone can learn the schema and test code before applying for full access.
items.access_note: Direct download under the Open Database License; no account needed.

items.name: MIMIC-IV-ED
items.description: Emergency department module of MIMIC-IV with ~425,000 ED stays: triage, vital signs, medication reconciliation, dispensed medications and diagnoses. Links to MIMIC-IV hospital and ICU records.
items.provider: MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology / BIDMC

items.name: MIMIC-IV-Note
items.description: De-identified free-text discharge summaries (~330,000) and radiology reports (~2.3 million) linked to MIMIC-IV patients — a major resource for clinical NLP and LLM research.
items.provider: MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology / BIDMC
items.access_note: PhysioNet credentialing + CITI training + DUA. Data must not be sent to third-party online LLM services.

items.name: MIMIC-IV-ECHO
items.description: Echocardiogram DICOM studies (~500,000 videos) from patients in MIMIC-IV, linkable to their EHR data and notes for multimodal cardiac research.
items.provider: MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology / BIDMC

items.name: eICU-CRD
items.description: Multi-centre ICU data for >200,000 admissions across 208 US hospitals (2014–2015) collected through the Philips eICU telehealth programme. Complements single-centre MIMIC for external validation.
items.access_note: PhysioNet credentialing + CITI training + DUA. An open demo subset is also available.

paper.label: Pollard TJ et al. Sci Data 2018;5:180178

items.name: AmsterdamUMCdb
items.description: The first freely accessible European ICU database: ~23,000 ICU admissions at Amsterdam UMC (2003–2016) with high-resolution vitals, ventilator settings, labs and drugs (~1 billion data points).
items.provider: Amsterdam UMC / Amsterdam Medical Data Science
items.access_note: Free; requires a short request, completion of human-subjects training and an End User License Agreement.

paper.label: Thoral PJ et al. Crit Care Med 2021;49:e563

items.name: HiRID
items.description: Data for ~34,000 ICU admissions at Bern University Hospital with physiological parameters sampled every 2 minutes — notably higher resolution than most ICU datasets. Developed for early warning of circulatory failure.

paper.label: Hyland SL et al. Nat Med 2020;26:364

items.name: SICdb
items.description: ICU data for ~27,000 admissions at University Hospital Salzburg (2013–2021) including per-minute vital signs, therapies, labs and cost-related information.

paper.label: Rodemund N et al. Intensive Care Med 2023;49:987

items.name: PIC
items.description: A large paediatric ICU database from the Children's Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine (2010–2018) covering ~13,000 children, structured similarly to MIMIC.

paper.label: Zeng X et al. Sci Data 2020;7:14

items.name: VitalDB
items.description: High-fidelity intraoperative data from 6,388 surgical patients at Seoul National University Hospital: synchronised waveforms (ECG, arterial pressure, EEG/BIS, ventilator), numeric vitals, anaesthetic drugs and perioperative clinical data.
items.access_note: Open download via vitaldb.net, Python API, or PhysioNet (open access).

paper.label: Lee HC et al. Sci Data 2022;9:279

items.name: INSPIRE
items.description: Perioperative research dataset of ~130,000 surgical cases from Seoul National University Hospital, combining intraoperative vitals with pre- and post-operative EHR data and outcomes.

paper.label: Lim L et al. Sci Data 2024;11:655

items.name: MC-MED
items.full_name: Multimodal Clinical Monitoring in the Emergency Department
items.description: 118,385 adult ED visits at Stanford (2020–2022) pairing continuous vitals and waveforms (ECG, PPG, respiration) with structured EHR data and radiology reports.

paper.label: Kansal A et al. Sci Data 2025

items.name: MOVER
items.full_name: Medical Informatics Operating Room Vitals and Events Repository
items.description: Operating-room data from ~58,000 surgical patients at UC Irvine Medical Center, including intraoperative waveforms, vitals, medications and perioperative EHR records.
items.access_note: Free download for anyone who signs the data usage agreement (via mover.ics.uci.edu or the UCI repository).

paper.label: Samad M et al. JAMIA Open 2023;6:ooad084

items.name: PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2019 (Sepsis)
items.description: Hourly ICU data for ~40,000 patients from three hospital systems, released for early prediction of sepsis. A compact, ready-to-model benchmark.

paper.label: Reyna MA et al. Crit Care Med 2020;48:210
